title: The Fox and the Crow - Birbal version (മലയാളം)
summary: Birbal retells the famous fable of the crow and the cheese to warn Akbar against a flattering foreign diplomat. [ML]
keywords: the fox and the crow - birbal version
full_text:
A clever and silver-tongued ambassador from a rival principality arrived at the court of Emperor Akbar. Bowing with dramatic flourishes, the diplomat spent two hours reciting lavish praise: 'O Emperor Akbar! Your face is brighter than the full moon! Your voice is sweeter than celestial harps! Your generosity outshines the sun itself!'

Akbar, basking in the intoxicating praise, was on the verge of signing an extraordinarily one-sided trade treaty that would have surrendered the revenues of three border provinces to the foreign kingdom.

Birbal stepped forward, bowed politely to the ambassador, and turned to Akbar: 'Sire, before you seal this treaty with the royal signet, allow me to recount the Birbal version of the Fox and the Crow.'

Akbar smiled: 'Speak, Birbal.'

Birbal narrated: 'A crow was perched upon a high oak branch, holding a delicious piece of spiced mutton in its beak. A hungry fox spotted the prize and sat at the foot of the tree.

'"O magnificent bird!" the fox called out with tears of admiration. "I have heard of your royal pedigree, but I never knew your feathers were as black and lustrous as silk! And they say that when you sing, even the nightingales weep with envy! Will you not bless my humble ears with one sweet song?"

'The vain crow, intoxicated by the flattery, puffed out its chest, opened its beak wide, and croaked with all its might: *Caw! Caw!*

'The instant its beak opened, the meat fell into the grass below. The fox snapped up the savory morsel, swallowed it down, and laughed: "Thank you for the feast, foolish bird! You have a voice like a rusty gate, but a mind even weaker than your voice!"'

Akbar paused. He looked down at the treaty scroll on his desk, and then at the sweet-talking foreign ambassador who was sweating nervously.

The Emperor laughed aloud at how Birbal had shattered the diplomat's spell: 'Thank you, Birbal! You have snatched the imperial cheese before the fox could carry it away!'

Akbar tore up the unfair treaty, negotiated strict and equitable terms, and rewarded Birbal for his timely vigilance.
